causal_chain: Adding a user-conditioned exclusion memory creates a second relation that accumulates directions repeatedly opposed by the user's observed comparisons.
Scoring candidates by attraction minus gated exclusion suppresses plausible-but-wrong substitutes that ordinary affinity models over-rank.
Standard single-channel pairwise recommenders compress these signals into one compatibility vector, so avoidance patterns are not preserved as reusable scoring structure.
Therefore a dual-memory attraction/exclusion recommender should improve NDCG@10 over matched single-relation controls under the same pairwise protocol.
This is most useful in full-sort ranking where many catalog items are near a user's liked region but differ along a repeatedly rejected facet.
User histories contain both attraction evidence and implicit avoidance evidence toward item regions.
blind_projection.closest_parent: Explicitly learning a user-conditioned exclusion memory and subtractive gate alongside standard attraction embeddings will improve ranking quality because many hard negatives are not merely low-affinity items; they are items that align with patterns the user's history implicitly avoids.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any improvement would come only from extra parameters or generic regularization rather than from modeling an explicit exclusion relation.
discriminative_predictions: A parameter-matched control that adds a second user embedding through additive fusion instead of subtractive exclusion will underperform the proposed mechanism if the exclusion relation is the operative cause.

Replacing user-specific exclusion memory with a single global exclusion vector should remove most of the gain while keeping similar regularization pressure, indicating the effect is not just extra capacity.

The proposed model should show larger relative improvement for users whose histories span nearby but conflicting item neighborhoods, whereas a generic-capacity explanation predicts more uniform gains across users.
expected_evidence: Ablation removing subtractive exclusion should collapse performance toward the matched control more than toward random variation.
Higher full-sort NDCG@10 than BPR-MF and than a parameter-matched additive two-embedding control.
Reduced scores for popular substitute items that share broad affinity structure with positives but align with learned exclusion directions.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a parameter-matched additive control or global-exclusion control matches or exceeds the proposed model on NDCG@10, the exclusion-relation hypothesis is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: The proposal introduces an explicit second user-item relation with subtractive scoring semantics and dedicated updates from negative evidence, which changes the representational object from single compatibility to attraction-plus-opposition rather than merely retuning an existing operator.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A pairwise-trained recommender that learns both user attraction embeddings and user-conditioned exclusion embeddings, then scores each candidate by direct affinity minus a bounded exclusion penalty, will improve full-sort NDCG@10 over single-relation collaborative filters because it can suppress hard substitute items that resemble liked items along globally common factors but repeatedly conflict with the user's implicit avoided facets.
implementation_requirements: Add a mechanism-off ablation by fixing the exclusion penalty to zero, recovering the single-channel scorer.
Add a parameter-matched control variant with two user embeddings fused additively instead of subtractively.
Define score(u,i)=dot(a_u,v_i)-sigmoid(beta_u)*dot(e_u,v_i), with beta_u as a learned scalar or derived gate from user norms.
Evaluate with frozen full-sort NDCG@10 on the protocol split without any held-out-dependent fitting.
Implement a PyTorch recommender with user attraction embeddings, user exclusion embeddings, and shared item embeddings.
Optimize a BPR-style pairwise loss on score(u,pos)-score(u,neg) plus regularization for attraction, exclusion, and gate parameters.
Use pairwise triples (user, positive item, negative item) only from the training split.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a parameter-matched two-user-embedding control with identical optimizer, sampler, embedding sizes, and regularization budget, but combine the second embedding additively rather than as a subtractive exclusion channel.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce an explicit user-conditioned opposition memory that is learned from pairwise comparisons and enters inference through subtractive gating against item affinity.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Set the exclusion branch contribution to zero for all users while keeping the same attraction embeddings, item embeddings, optimizer, and training data; this reduces the model to the single-channel pairwise scorer and isolates the value of explicit exclusion memory.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: Add one exclusion embedding per user plus a bounded subtractive gate on top of a standard matrix-factorization pairwise scorer, and compare against both the mechanism-off version and a parameter-matched additive control.
blind_projection.research_question: Does adding a user-specific exclusion memory with subtractive gating yield better full-sort NDCG@10 than single-relation pairwise collaborative filtering under the frozen ML-1M protocol?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The model is lightweight relative to graph-based recommenders: one extra user embedding table and a simple gated subtraction should keep training near BPR-MF cost and within the stated development budget on ML-1M.
